L04 Maps

Data Visualization (STAT 302)

Author

Yizhe Zhang

Github Repo Link

https://github.com/yzh349/Stat302.git

Overview

The goal of this lab is to explore various ways of building maps with ggplot2.

Challenges are not mandatory for students to complete. We highly recommend students attempt them though. We would expect graduate students to attempt the challenges.

Datasets

We’ll be using the US_income.rda dataset which should be placed in the data/ subdirectory in our L04 project. You’ll also be downloading your own data to build maps.

Code 
# Load package(s)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tidycensus)
library(mapview)
library(tigris)
library(geodata)
library(raster)
library(janitor)
library(maps)
library(viridis)
library(statebins)
#resolve conflicted functions
conflicted::conflict_prefer("select","dplyr")
conflicted::conflict_prefer("filter","dplyr")

# Load dataset(s)
load(file = "US_income.rda")

Exercise 1

Plot 1

Make a county map of a US state using geom_polygon(). Maybe use your home state or a favorite state. Please do NOT use the state in the ggplot2 book example.

Optional: Consider adding major cities (or your home town).

Hints:

  • See section 6.1 in our book.
  • Void theme
TipSolution
Code 
ny_counties <- map_data("county" , "new york") %>%
  select(lon = long, lat, group, id = subregion)
  ggplot(ny_counties, aes(lon, lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = NA, color = "grey50") +
  coord_quickmap() +
  ggtitle("NewYork") +
  theme_void()

Plot 2

Now use geom_sf() instead. You’ll need to download data for this. You can use either the tigris (github page) or geodata packages. Either tigris’ counties() with cb = TRUE or geodata’s gadm() could be useful.

TipSolution
Code 
usa_dat <- gadm(country = "USA" , level = 2, path = tempdir()) %>%
  st_as_sf()%>%
  clean_names()
ny_data <- usa_dat %>%
  filter(name_1 == "New York")
ggplot(ny_data) +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, color = "grey50") +
  theme_void() + 
  ggtitle("New York")

Exercise 2

Using the US_income dataset, recreate the following graphics as precisely as possible.

Code 
# Setting income levels
US_income <- mutate(
  US_income,
  income_bins = cut(
    ifelse(is.na(median_income), 25000, median_income),
    breaks = c(0, 40000, 50000, 60000, 70000, 80000),
    labels = c("< $40k", "$40k to $50k", 
               "$50k to $60k", "$60k to $70k", "> $70k"),
    right = FALSE
  )
)

Plot 1

Hints:

  • geom_sf() — boundary color is "grey80" and size is 0.2
  • viridis package (discrete = TRUE in scale_* function)
  • Void theme
TipSolution
Code 
ggplot(US_income, aes(fill = income_bins, geometry = geometry)) + geom_sf(color = "grey80" , size = 0.2) + 
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
  labs(fill = "median\nincome")

Plot 2

Hints:

  • statebins::geom_statebins()
  • viridis package (discrete = TRUE in scale_* function)
  • Statebins theme
Tip
Code 
ggplot(US_income, aes(state = name, fill = income_bins)) +
  geom_statebins() +
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
  theme_statebins() +
  labs(fill = "median\nincome")

Exercise 3

Pick any city or foreign country to build a map for. You can dress it up or make it as basic as you want. Also welcome to try building a graphic like that depicted at the end of section 6.5 — use a different region though.

TipSolution
Code 
chn <- gadm(country = "CHN" , level = 1, path = tempdir()) %>%
  st_as_sf()
ggplot(chn) +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, color = "grey50") +
  theme_void() +
  ggtitle("Map of China")
